title: At university
summary: Daniel goes to a lecture at Cairo University and learns the verbal noun: الْقِرَاءَة (reading), الْكِتَابَة (writing), الدِّرَاسَة (studying).
intro: Layla takes Daniel to a lecture at Cairo University. To talk about activities, Arabic uses the verbal noun (maṣdar), the '-ing' word of English: قَرَأَ (read) → الْقِرَاءَة (reading), كَتَبَ (wrote) → الْكِتَابَة (writing), دَرَسَ (studied) → الدِّرَاسَة (studying). أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَة means 'I love reading'.
objectives: Name places and people at a university
Turn five verbs into verbal nouns, such as قَرَأَ → قِرَاءَة
Say what you love doing with أُحِبُّ + a verbal noun
Ask and answer a question in a lecture

realLife.title: A lecture in a big hall
realLife.story: The lecture hall at Cairo University has three hundred seats, and most of them are full. The professor speaks without notes and quotes old poems by heart. Daniel writes the words he doesn't know in his notebook, and after the lecture he finds the courage to ask a question.

sentences.literal: I love the reading and the writing

mistakes.why: dirāsa (studying) is feminine, so the adjective takes ة: mumtiʿa.

sentences.en: The lecture is in the Faculty of Arts.
sentences.literal: the lecture (is) in (the) faculty (of) the arts

sentences.en: The student asks, and the professor answers.
sentences.literal: the student asks, and the professor answers

sentences.en: I have an exam in Arabic literature.
sentences.literal: at me an exam in the Arabic literature
I love that I read the poetry

mistakes.why: Two verbs cannot stand side by side: put an between them (the second ends in -a), or use the verbal noun: uḥibbu qirāʾata sh-shiʿr.

dialogue.title: A lecture on Arabic poetry
dialogue.culture: Cairo University, founded in 1908, is one of the oldest and largest universities in the Arab world. Arabs are proud of their poetry: poets such as al-Mutanabbi, who lived a thousand years ago, are still quoted, and many people know whole poems by heart. Students call a woman professor يَا دُكْتُورَة.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا دَانْيَال! هٰذِهِ كُلِّيَّةُ الْآدَاب فِي جَامِعَةِ الْقَاهِرَة. الْمُحَاضَرَة تَبْدَأُ بَعْدَ عَشْرِ دَقَائِق.
lines.en: Good morning, Daniel! This is the Faculty of Arts at Cairo University. The lecture starts in ten minutes.

lines.ar: الْجَامِعَة كَبِيرَة جِدًّا! كَمْ طَالِبًا يَدْرُسُ هُنَا؟ وَمَا مَوْضُوعُ الْمُحَاضَرَةِ الْيَوْم؟
lines.en: The university is really big! How many students study here? And what is the topic of today's lecture?

lines.ar: يَدْرُسُ هُنَا آلَافُ الطُّلَّاب. وَالْمُحَاضَرَة عَنِ الْأَدَبِ الْعَرَبِيّ، وَالْأُسْتَاذَة هِيَ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى.
lines.en: Thousands of students study here. And the lecture is about Arabic literature; the professor is Dr Mona.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا طُلَّاب. الْيَوْم نَتَكَلَّمُ عَنْ قِرَاءَةِ الشِّعْرِ الْعَرَبِيّ. الْقِرَاءَة مُهِمَّة، وَالْكِتَابَة أَيْضًا.
lines.en: Good morning, students. Today we're talking about reading Arabic poetry. Reading is important, and so is writing.

lines.ar: يَا لَيْلَى، الدُّكْتُورَة تَتَكَلَّمُ بِسُرْعَة! أَنَا أَفْهَمُ نِصْفَ الْكَلَام فَقَطْ.
lines.en: Layla, the professor is speaking so fast! I only understand half of what she says.

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. اُكْتُبِ الْكَلِمَات الصَّعْبَة فِي دَفْتَرِكَ، وَبَعْدَ الْمُحَاضَرَة نَسْأَلُهَا عَنْهَا.
lines.en: No problem. Write the difficult words in your notebook, and after the lecture we'll ask her about them.

lines.ar: مَنْ يَعْرِفُ شَاعِرًا عَرَبِيًّا مَشْهُورًا؟ نَعَم، أَنْتَ هُنَاكَ فِي آخِرِ الْقَاعَة.
lines.en: Who knows a famous Arab poet? Yes, you over there at the back of the hall.

lines.ar: أَنَا أَعْرِفُ الْمُتَنَبِّي. قَرَأْتُ قَصِيدَة لَهُ فِي دَرْسِ الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم فِي مَدْرَسَةِ اللُّغَة.
lines.en: I know al-Mutanabbi. I read one of his poems in Mr Karim's lesson at the language school.

lines.ar: إِجَابَة مُمْتَازَة! مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ عَرَبِيَّتُكَ جَيِّدَة جِدًّا. هَلْ دِرَاسَةُ الْعَرَبِيَّة صَعْبَة عَلَيْكَ؟
lines.en: An excellent answer! Where are you from? Your Arabic is very good. Is studying Arabic hard for you?

lines.ar: أَنَا مِنْ شِيكَاغُو فِي أَمْرِيكَا. الدِّرَاسَة صَعْبَة قَلِيلًا، لٰكِنِّي أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَة وَالْكِتَابَة بِالْعَرَبِيَّة كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: I'm from Chicago in America. Studying is a little hard, but I really love reading and writing in Arabic.

lines.ar: أَحْسَنْتَ! يَا طُلَّاب، عِنْدَكُمُ امْتِحَان بَعْدَ أُسْبُوعَيْنِ. اِقْرَؤُوا الْقَصَائِد فِي الْكِتَاب قَبْلَ الْمُحَاضَرَةِ الْقَادِمَة.
lines.en: Well done! Students, you have an exam in two weeks. Read the poems in the book before the next lecture.

lines.ar: يَا دُكْتُورَة، عِنْدِي سُؤَال: مَا مَعْنَى كَلِمَة دِيوَان؟ كَتَبْتُهَا فِي دَفْتَرِي، لٰكِنِّي لَا أَفْهَمُهَا.
lines.en: Doctor, I have a question: what does the word 'diwan' mean? I wrote it in my notebook, but I don't understand it.

lines.ar: الدِّيوَان كِتَاب فِيهِ قَصَائِدُ شَاعِر وَاحِد. سُؤَال جَيِّد! يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَحْضُرَ الْمُحَاضَرَة كُلَّ أُسْبُوع.
lines.en: A diwan is a book with the poems of one poet. A good question! You can come to the lecture every week.

lines.ar: أَرَأَيْتَ يَا دَانْيَال؟ سَأَلْتَ، وَأَجَابَتِ الدُّكْتُورَة، وَالْآنَ أَنْتَ طَالِب فِي الْجَامِعَة أَيْضًا!
lines.en: You see, Daniel? You asked, the professor answered, and now you're a university student as well!

reading.title: A lecture at Cairo University
reading.ar: ذَهَبَ دَانْيَال مَعَ لَيْلَى إِلَى جَامِعَةِ الْقَاهِرَة. حَضَرَا مُحَاضَرَة عَنِ الشِّعْرِ الْعَرَبِيّ فِي كُلِّيَّةِ الْآدَاب. الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى تَتَكَلَّمُ بِسُرْعَة، فَكَتَبَ دَانْيَال الْكَلِمَات الصَّعْبَة فِي دَفْتَرِهِ. بَعْدَ الْمُحَاضَرَة سَأَلَ دَانْيَال سُؤَالًا، وَأَجَابَتِ الدُّكْتُورَة. دَانْيَال يُحِبُّ الدِّرَاسَة فِي الْجَامِعَة.
reading.en: Daniel went with Layla to Cairo University. They attended a lecture on Arabic poetry in the Faculty of Arts. Dr Mona speaks fast, so Daniel wrote the difficult words in his notebook. After the lecture Daniel asked a question, and the professor answered. Daniel loves studying at the university.

quiz.prompt: Which is the verbal noun of قَرَأَ (read)?

options: a book with the poems of one poet

quiz.prompt: Which word has a long ā?

completion: Excellent! You can talk about university life and use verbal nouns like الْقِرَاءَة and الْكِتَابَة. Next, Daniel answers the phone at the office.
